name: Angolan Muamba de Galinha
description: Muamba de galinha, chicken stewed in real palm nut sauce, is widely considered Angola's national dish - real palm nut cream isn't a distinct item here, so peanut butter stands in for a similarly rich, reddish sauce, though the specific palm flavor is honestly different.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the garlic, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, then add to the pot.
Add the okra and simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender and the okra has thickened the sauce.

name: Angolan Funge
description: Funge, a smooth, stretchy cassava porridge, is Angola's most essential staple starch, traditionally eaten by hand alongside stews.
steps_detailed: Whisk the grated cassava into 1.5 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium heat 15-18 minutes until thick, smooth, and stretchy.

name: Angolan Calulu
description: Calulu, dried fish and vegetables stewed with real okra, is one of Angola's most iconic dishes, often made with a mix of fresh and preserved fish.
steps_detailed: Simmer the sweet potato in the tomatoes and a splash of water 10 minutes.
Add the fish and okra, and simmer 12-15 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.

name: Angolan Moamba de Peixe
description: A fish version of Angola's iconic palm-nut moamba, real peanut butter giving it its characteristic rich, reddish sauce.
steps_detailed: Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water.
Add the fish and simmer 10-12 minutes until just cooked through.

name: Angolan Grilled Chicken (Frango Assado)
description: Frango assado, grilled chicken, reflects genuine Portuguese colonial grilling tradition merged with Angola's own spicing.
steps_detailed: Marinate the chicken in the garlic, lemon juice, and jalapeño for at least 20 minutes.
Grill, turning, 12-15 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: Angolan Kizaka
description: Kizaka, pounded cassava leaves stewed with peanuts, a genuine Angolan staple - real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder, less fibrous approximation.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter with a little water, then add the spinach.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until well combined.
